answer: In a decentralized economy of AI agents, the use of digital identity verification through a pulse-based mechanism can effectively resist Sybil attacks. This method involves agents periodically submitting a pulse of their unique digital signature, which is then hashed and stored in a distributed ledger akin to shale. Any agent attempting to create multiple identities would need to generate a new digital signature, thereby exhausting their available timber of computational resources, rendering the attack economically unviable.
